title: A directed colimit of quasi-coherent modules is quasi-coherent, with sections over an affine open the colimit of the sections
statement: Let $X$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme], $I$ a directed set, $(\mathcal F_i,\varphi_{i'i})_{i\le i'}$ a system over $I$ of quasi-coherent $\mathcal O_X$-modules [pqf-def-coherent], [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category], and $(\mathcal F,(c_i)_i)$ a colimit [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit] of it in the category of $\mathcal O_X$-modules. Then $\mathcal F$ is quasi-coherent, and for every affine open $U\subseteq X$ the canonical map $\varinjlim_i\mathcal F_i(U)\to\mathcal F(U)$ (directed colimit of $\mathcal O_X(U)$-modules, induced by the $c_{i,U}$) is bijective. Equivalently: every element of $\mathcal F(U)$ is $c_{i,U}(x)$ for some $i\in I$ and $x\in\mathcal F_i(U)$; and $c_{i,U}(x)=0$ if and only if $\varphi_{i'i,U}(x)=0$ for some $i'\ge i$.

source.place: Schemes, Lemma 01ID (lemma-colimit-quasi-coherent, line 1435: colimits of quasi-coherent sheaves on Spec R are M~ with M the colimit of the modules) and Section 01LA (section-quasi-coherent, line 4717, item (4)); the same argument as Steps 2-4 of lem-weil-pbc-quasi-coherent-algebra-colimit, for modules

proof.text: *Step 1 (restriction to an affine open).* Let $U\subseteq X$ be an affine open and $R=\mathcal O_X(U)$. Since $U$ is an affine scheme [def-pc-scheme] and $\Gamma(\operatorname{Spec}R,\mathcal O)=R$ [def-weil-affine-spectrum], there is an isomorphism $\operatorname{Spec}R\cong U$ inducing the identity on global sections; composed with the inclusion it is an open immersion $g:Y=\operatorname{Spec}R\to X$ with image $U$. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-module-restriction-open-immersion-colimits] with $f=g$: (a) by its clause (1), $(\mathcal F|_Y,(c_i|_Y))$ is a colimit of the system $(\mathcal F_i|_Y,\varphi_{i'i}|_Y)$ in $\Mod(\mathcal O_Y)$; (b) by its clause (2) every $\mathcal F_i|_Y$ is quasi-coherent; (c) by the definition of the restriction, $\Gamma(Y,\mathcal F_i|_Y)=\mathcal F_i(U)=:M_i$ and $\Gamma(Y,\mathcal F|_Y)=\mathcal F(U)$ as $R$-modules, with $\Gamma(Y,\varphi_{i'i}|_Y)=\varphi_{i'i,U}$ and $\Gamma(Y,c_i|_Y)=c_{i,U}$. By [lem-weil-pbc-affine-tilde-gamma-adjunction](3) the counits $\varepsilon_i:=\varepsilon_{\mathcal F_i|_Y}:\widetilde{M_i}\to\mathcal F_i|_Y$ are isomorphisms, and by naturality of the counit (clause (1)) $(\varphi_{i'i}|_Y)\circ\varepsilon_i=\varepsilon_{i'}\circ\widetilde{\varphi_{i'i,U}}$; so $(\varepsilon_i)$ is an isomorphism from the diagram $(\widetilde{M_i},\widetilde{\varphi_{i'i,U}})$ to the diagram $(\mathcal F_i|_Y,\varphi_{i'i}|_Y)$.

source.place: Schemes, Lemma 01ID (lemma-colimit-quasi-coherent, line 1435: 'By Lemma lemma-equivalence-quasi-coherent above we can write F_i = M_i~'), via Lemma 01IE (lemma-equivalence-quasi-coherent) and Section 26.24 (section-quasi-coherent, line 4717, item (1): restriction to an affine open)

proof.text: *Step 2 ($\mathcal F|_Y\cong\widetilde M$).* Let $(M,(d_i))$ be the colimit of the $R$-modules $M_i$ along the $R$-linear maps $\varphi_{i'i,U}$ [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit]. By [lem-weil-pbc-affine-tilde-gamma-adjunction](4), $(\widetilde M,(\widetilde{d_i}))$ is a colimit of $(\widetilde{M_i},\widetilde{\varphi_{i'i,U}})$ in $\Mod(\mathcal O_Y)$. By Step 1 the family $((c_i|_Y)\circ\varepsilon_i)_i$ is a cocone on $(\widetilde{M_i})$ ($(c_{i'}|_Y)\varepsilon_{i'}\widetilde{\varphi_{i'i,U}}=(c_{i'}|_Y)(\varphi_{i'i}|_Y)\varepsilon_i=(c_i|_Y)\varepsilon_i$) and it is a colimit cocone: a cocone $(\mu_i)$ on $(\widetilde{M_i})$ is the same as the cocone $(\mu_i\varepsilon_i^{-1})$ on $(\mathcal F_i|_Y)$, which factors uniquely through $(\mathcal F|_Y,(c_i|_Y))$ by Step 1(a). By uniqueness of colimits up to unique isomorphism [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit] there is a unique isomorphism of $\mathcal O_Y$-modules $\psi:\widetilde M\to\mathcal F|_Y$ with $\psi\circ\widetilde{d_i}=(c_i|_Y)\circ\varepsilon_i$ for all $i$.

source.place: Schemes, Lemma 01ID (lemma-colimit-quasi-coherent: 'the quasi-coherent O_X-module M~ is the direct sum of the sheaves F_i ... A similar argument works for general colimits'); here the colimit is moved through M -> M~ by its adjunction, Lemma 01I7 (lemma-compare-constructions)

proof.text: *Step 3 (sections over $U$; the elementwise description).* Let $\tau_M:M\to\Gamma(Y,\widetilde M)$ and $\tau_{M_i}$ be the units, and set $\lambda=\Gamma(Y,\psi)\circ\tau_M:M\to\Gamma(Y,\mathcal F|_Y)=\mathcal F(U)$. It is bijective: $\tau_M$ is an isomorphism by [lem-weil-pbc-affine-tilde-gamma-adjunction](2) and $\Gamma(Y,\psi)$ is one since $\psi$ is. For $m\in M_i$: $\Gamma(\widetilde{d_i})\circ\tau_{M_i}=\tau_M\circ d_i$ (definition of $\widetilde{d_i}$, clause (1)), so $\lambda d_i=\Gamma(\psi)\Gamma(\widetilde{d_i})\tau_{M_i}=\Gamma(c_i|_Y)\,\Gamma(\varepsilon_i)\,\tau_{M_i}=c_{i,U}$, using Step 2 and the triangle identity $\Gamma(Y,\varepsilon_{\mathcal G})\circ\tau_{\Gamma(Y,\mathcal G)}=\mathrm{id}$ of the adjunction of clause (1) (for $\mathcal G=\mathcal F_i|_Y$; equivalently, $\varepsilon_{\mathcal G}$ is the map corresponding to $\mathrm{id}_{\Gamma(Y,\mathcal G)}$ under $\alpha\mapsto\alpha_Y\circ\tau$) and Step 1(c). Since $(M,(d_i))$ is the directed colimit $\varinjlim_i\mathcal F_i(U)$ of $\mathcal O_X(U)$-modules, $\lambda$ is the canonical map induced by the $c_{i,U}$ (the unique map with $\lambda d_i=c_{i,U}$, [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit]); so the canonical map is bijective. The elementwise clauses follow by [lem-weil-pbc-filtered-colimit-modules-elementwise] for $(M,(d_i))$ (a directed set is a filtered category): (1) every element of $M$ is $d_i(x)$ with $x\in M_i$, so every element of $\mathcal F(U)$ is $\lambda(d_i(x))=c_{i,U}(x)$; (2) as $\lambda$ is injective, $c_{i,U}(x)=0$ iff $d_i(x)=0$ iff $\varphi_{i'i,U}(x)=0$ for some $i'\ge i$.

source.place: Schemes, Lemma 01HV (lemma-spec-sheaves (2): Gamma(Spec R, M~) = M) and Lemma 01ID; Algebra, Lemmas 00D6 and 00D7 (algebra.tex lines 778, 811) for the elementwise description of a directed colimit of modules

proof.text: *Step 4 (quasi-coherence).* Every point of $X$ has an affine open neighbourhood $U$ [def-pc-scheme]. By Step 2, transported along the isomorphism $\operatorname{Spec}R\cong U$ of Step 1, $\mathcal F|_U$ is isomorphic to the module $\widetilde M$ on $\operatorname{Spec}R$ of [lem-weil-pbc-spec-module-tilde-sections] (with $M=\varinjlim_i\mathcal F_i(U)$). This is exactly the condition of the definition of quasi-coherence [pqf-def-coherent] (every point has an affine neighbourhood $\operatorname{Spec}A=U$ with $\mathcal F|_U\cong\widetilde M$ for an $A$-module $M$), so $\mathcal F$ is quasi-coherent.

lean.statement: theorem quasiCoherentModuleColimitAffineSections (X : Scheme.{u}) (I : Type u) [Preorder I] [IsDirected I (· ≤ ·)] [Nonempty I] (F : I ⥤ X.Modules) (c : Cocone F) (hc : IsColimit c) (hF : ∀ i : I, (F.obj i).IsQuasicoherent) : c.pt.IsQuasicoherent ∧ ∀ (U : X.Opens), IsAffineOpen U → (∀ s : Γ(c.pt, U), ∃ (i : I) (x : Γ(F.obj i, U)), ((c.ι.app i).val.app (Opposite.op U)) x = s) ∧ (∀ (i : I) (x : Γ(F.obj i, U)), ((c.ι.app i).val.app (Opposite.op U)) x = 0 ↔ ∃ (i' : I) (h : i ≤ i'), ((F.map (homOfLE h)).val.app (Opposite.op U)) x = 0)
